guides.label: Asking well
guides.title: Say what you want, and what done looks like.
guides.lead: Tempo is a band that plays on your machine. Give it a clear cue and it plays the right part.
body: Name the folder or the file. Say what you want at the end: a list, a fix, a summary.
If the job has steps, say the order. Tempo keeps a task list and ticks it off.
Not sure? Ask for a plan first. That is the rehearsal, and it changes nothing.
examples: Look in {folder} and tell me which three files matter most, and why.
Fix the failing test in {file}. Show me the change before you make it.
Write me a one-page summary of {topic} from my notes, with sources.

guides.label: Approvals
guides.title: Tempo asks before it changes anything.
guides.lead: Reading is free. Changing asks first.
body: Anything that writes, installs, uses the network or goes to the trash shows a card with what it will do. Approve, or deny.
Deleting is refused outright. The trash is the only way out, and the file can come back.
In accept-edits mode, file edits inside your write folders go ahead. Commands and new websites still ask.
examples: Use trash to move {a file} to the trash.

guides.label: The rehearsal: plan mode
guides.title: The rehearsal: plan mode.
guides.lead: A dry run: Tempo reads and thinks, and touches nothing. (Plan mode)
body: Use it on anything that worries you. Tempo reads, then hands you a numbered plan.
When the plan is right, switch with /mode default and say go.
/plan with a task plans that task in one step.
examples: /plan move my notes into one folder per year

guides.label: /undo
guides.title: Take it back. /undo puts files back.
guides.lead: Every changing turn keeps what the files held before.
body: /diff shows what the last changing turn changed.
/undo puts those files back. The newer versions go to the trash, not away.
It covers edits and patches. Commands you ran with run_command are on you, so look first.

guides.label: @file
guides.title: Point at a file with @.
guides.lead: Type @ and a path, and the file goes into the message.
body: Handy for a log, a config or a draft. Tempo reads it as part of your question.
For a whole folder, ask for list_dir or grep instead.
!command runs a command yourself and puts its output in the chat.
examples: Explain what @{file} does, in plain words.

guides.label: Background commands
guides.title: Let long jobs play on their own.
guides.lead: A dev server or a slow build should not hold up the chat.
body: Ask Tempo to run it in the background. You get an id like bg-1 straight away.
Check on it with command_output, end it with command_stop, or /stop.
/status lists what is running. Nothing outlives Tempo.
examples: Run {the dev server} in the background and tell me when it is up.

guides.label: Hooks
guides.title: Hooks: your own checks around Tempo's steps.
guides.lead: A hook is a command of yours that runs before a tool, after a tool or after a turn.
body: Block a risky command, run a formatter after every edit, ping yourself when a turn ends.
They live in your settings file under hooks. Exit code 2 blocks the step.
Ask Tempo to help you write one. It will show the settings change before it makes it.
examples: Help me write a hook that runs {my formatter} after every edit.
Help me write a hook that blocks {a command} before run_command.

guides.label: Soundcheck
guides.title: Soundcheck before you go live.
guides.lead: Review for code and security: scanners first, then four listens and a second listen.
body: /soundcheck looks at what changed in this folder. /review is the same thing.
Name a target to narrow it: a commit, a folder, a file.
Fix what it finds, then run it again. That is the encore.

guides.label: The Conductor
guides.title: The Conductor sets up your band.
guides.lead: A band is a small team of AI members for one workflow. Each plays on the engine that suits the part.
body: Start from a template, or describe your workflow in a sentence.
A flow is the setlist: its steps, in order, run when you say or on a schedule.
Type / and pick a band to cue a flow from here.
examples: Explain how the Conductor sets up a band for {my workflow}.
Run the {flow} flow of the {band} band.
Which of my bands has a flow that runs every week?

guides.label: The Fleet
guides.title: The Fleet: every machine in one field.
guides.lead: Tempo can hand a small job to another machine of yours.
body: delegate gives a read-only job to a machine that has the model for it.
Each read it makes asks you first, unless you trusted that machine in your settings.
Ask which machine is best for a job, and Tempo says why.
examples: Use delegate to ask {a machine} to {summarise a folder}.
Which of my machines should make images?

guides.label: Vault
guides.title: The Vault is your memory, in plain files.
guides.lead: Notes as Markdown, readable by you and by Tempo, on your computer.
body: Tempo cites the note it used, so you can check it.
Ask it to link, tidy or summarise. Overwriting a note asks first.
Ctrl+K in the Vault lists every command it has.
examples: Use search_memory to find what I wrote about {a topic}.
Which of my notes link to each other the most?
